newsitem.title: FRANCE: Aerospatiale to talk to Lagardere on Thomson - paper.
newsitem.headline: Aerospatiale to talk to Lagardere on Thomson - paper.

text.p: The French government has asked state-owned Aerospatiale to remain neutral in the bidding between Lagardere Groupe and Alcatel Alsthom for defence electronics firm Thomson-CSF, newspaper Le Monde reoprted on Monday.

"It is not a question of (Aerospatiale chairman) Yves Michot indicating his preference but advising the government on the industrial and strategic synergies of the two candidates," the newspaper quoted a defence ministry official as saying.
Aerospatiale has accepted that role, despite a history of antagonism between itself and Lagardere, it reported.

"We have to accept that we will talk to Lagardere, a predator which has for several years sworn to harm us and wanted to buy our missiles and satellites businesses," the report quoted an Aerospatiale executive as saying.

Le Monde reported that French President Jacques Chirac invited Lagardere chairman Jean-Luc Lagardere on his tour of South America, along with Michot, and that the two chairmen ended up talking to each other on the presidential flight.

The government has said Aerospatiale cannot take part in the Thomson-CSF sale but Michot's opinion would be canvassed on the rival offers as the outcome would have an effect on the state-owned aerospace group's business.

Lagardere and Aerospatiale compete directly in missiles and satellites and two years ago, Lagardere led a highly-public campaign to buy Aerospatiale's satellite plant at Cannes, on the French Riviera, as part of a plan to be the French centre of a pan-European space grouping.

Engineering company Alcatel has teamed up with Dassault Industrie, which holds the Dassault family's interest in Dassault Aviation, for a joint bid and has agreed to involve Aerospatiale if it wins Thomson-CSF.
